facts.raw_span: A 39-year-old female teacher from Southwest China presented with a subcutaneous mass in the lower-left abdominal region
a history of chronic urticaria (relieved by occasional use of loratadine)
cesarean section eight years ago
myomectomy to remove a myoma six months ago
denied a history of dysmenorrhea and abortion
The mass was accompanied by slight pain that worsened around menstruation
Heart, lungs, and abdomen showed no obvious abnormalities
No palpable swelling of superficial lymph nodes was noted
A subcutaneous nodule of approximately 1 cm diameter was present under the hypogastrium
The nodule's surface was normal, without ulceration or bleeding
Ultrasonography: Showed a hybrid echo-mass about 1.1 × 1.0 cm, with an irregular shape, well-defined border, located 3 mm from the body surface in the subcutaneous soft tissue
Histopathology: Revealed endometrial glands consisting of a single layer of monomorphous cuboidal cells with an endometrial stroma
